english.title: Sponsor fail to ensure the reporting of suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions in a clinical trial

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the sponsor of a clinical trial, failed to ensure that all relevant information about a suspected unexpected serious adverse reaction, which occurred during the course of the clinical trial in the United Kingdom and was fatal or life-threatening was reported to the licensing authority as soon as possible and in any event not later than 7 days after you were first aware of the reaction
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 33(1), 49(1)(h) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence applies from the 28th April 2026 due to changes made by the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) (Amendment) Regulations 2025. For the offence applicable before this date, see see H22173.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
